s: Which of the below mentioned freedom fighters was the founder of Andhra Bank?
After which movement was Tanguturi Prakasam called Andhra Kesari?
x:
During the Simon Commission protests held at Madras in 1928, Tanguturi Prakasam Pantulu displayed extraordinary courage by confronting armed British police. When the police threatened to fire on the protesters, Prakasam boldly opened his shirt and challenged them to shoot him. His fearless act inspired thousands of freedom fighters and earned him the title "Andhra Kesari" (Lion of Andhra). He later became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State after its formation in 1953.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Who was the President of Andhra Mahasabha between 1941–1946?
x:
M. Suryanarayana served as the President of the Andhra Mahasabha during the period 1941–1946. During this phase, the Andhra Mahasabha expanded its activities among the people of the Hyderabad State and became increasingly involved in raising issues relating to education, civil rights, social reforms and the welfare of peasants. In later years, the organization also played an important role in mobilizing public opinion against the autocratic rule of the Nizam. The Andhra Mahasabha occupies an important place in the political history of Telangana and Hyderabad State.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: In which year did Pingali Venkayya design the tricolour that was later adopted as the National Flag of India with minor modifications?
x:
Pingali Venkayya, a freedom fighter from Andhra Pradesh, designed the Indian National Flag in 1921. He presented the design to Mahatma Gandhi during the All India Congress Committee Session at Bezwada (Vijayawada). Gandhi suggested the inclusion of the spinning wheel (Charkha) in the centre. Later, on 22 July 1947, the Constituent Assembly adopted the present National Flag by replacing the Charkha with the Ashoka Chakra, while retaining the tricolour design.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Under whose leadership did the Peasant and Agrarian Movements take place in Andhra?
x:
Prof. N. G. Ranga was the foremost leader of the Peasant and Agrarian Movements in Andhra. He founded several farmers' organizations, including the Ryot Associations, and later played a leading role in the All India Kisan Sabha. His efforts focused on protecting farmers' rights, reducing land revenue and improving rural conditions. Because of his lifelong service to farmers, he is popularly known as the "Father of the Indian Peasant Movement."
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Who started the English daily "Swarajya"?
x:
Tanguturi Prakasam Pantulu founded the English daily Swarajya in 1921. The newspaper became a powerful voice of the Indian National Movement, criticizing British policies and spreading nationalist ideas. It played an important role in mobilizing public opinion during the freedom struggle.

s: Who was the first Telugu person to preside over the Indian National Congress?
x:
Dr. Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya became the first Telugu leader to serve as the President of the Indian National Congress. He was elected President at the Jaipur Session of the Indian National Congress in 1948. He was also a distinguished freedom fighter, historian and close associate of Mahatma Gandhi.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Who was the first President of the Andhra Congress Circle?
x:
Konda Venkatappayya became the first President of the Andhra Congress Circle, which was formed to organize and strengthen the Indian National Congress in the Telugu- speaking districts of the Madras Presidency. He was one of the leading freedom fighters of Andhra and played an important role in the Andhra movement.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who wrote History of the Indian National Congress?
x:
Dr. Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya authored the authoritative work History of the Indian National Congress. The book chronicles the growth of the Congress from its establishment in 1885 and is considered an important reference for the history of the Indian freedom movement.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
n: Book – History of the Indian National Congress

s: Who was appointed as the Dictator of the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra?
x:
Konda Venkatappayya was appointed as the Dictator (chief organizer) of the Civil Disobedience Movement in Andhra in 1930. He coordinated the movement after the launch of Gandhi's Salt Satyagraha.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Which of the following is incorrectly paired?
x:
The title "Desoddharaka" was actually conferred upon Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao Pantulu, the founder of Andhra Patrika, for his immense contribution to Telugu journalism, nationalism and public service. The remaining pairs are correct: • Deshabhakta – Konda Venkatappayya • Andhra Ratna – Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah • Andhra Kesari – Tanguturi Prakasam
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
